text:
maria-engsec: Heads-up: Security triage for a few Go module issues we just pulled in from OSS advisories (grpc, golang-jwt/oauth, net/http). I listed links in the thread. Can we decide pin/backport priority and a rollout plan?

tyler-sre: on it. are any of these exploitable in prod right now? which services call into the vulnerable codepaths?

sam-runtime: quick runbook: grpc CVE looks like RCE via malformed frames in the worst-case; we've seen a small uptick in client stream errors from inference-edge to model-hosts. oauth/jwt is token parsing/validation bug (medium). net/http patch is lower-priority (denial-ish edge case).

dependabot: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1324 updating google.golang.org/grpc -> v1.56.0 and github.com/golang-jwt/jwt -> v4.4.2 :rotating_light:

maria-engsec: thanks @dependabot. @sam-runtime can you confirm which repos need hotpatches vs scheduled patch? also legal/audit: do we need to flag any exported keys or KMS changes?

jessica-legal: flag the repos that have external customer integrations. we need audit entries for any key rotations, plus an advisory timeline for customers if we force a reissue. if KMS access tokens are involved, notify security ops.

sam-runtime: prioritization proposal: 1) model-hosts + inference-edge (hotpatch canary) 2) public api-gateway + oauth service (next-day patch) 3) internal admin services (schedule next sprint). net/http stays in backlog but add monitoring alert.

ashley-pm: timeline ok from product side if we can canary tomorrow morning and full roll by EOD. need rollback plan.

nate-eng: rollback plan: keep previous image tag in artifact repo, run canary traffic using routing flag, if errors > 1% revert via automated deploy job. CI should run integration + smoke + govulncheck.

maria-engsec: operational checklist I'm proposing (lightweight):
- create branch/PR for each repo with pinned versions
- run `govulncheck` and unit/integration suites in CI
- create canary deploy (5% traffic) with tracing enabled
- monitor errors & latency (SLOs) for 2 hours
- promote or roll back
- create audit log entry + KMS rotation note if any keys are exposed

Snippet to pin locally (put in PR):
```
# update modules and tidy
go get google.golang.org/grpc@v1.56.0
go get github.com/golang-jwt/jwt@v4.4.2
go mod tidy
# verify
govulncheck ./... || true
```

git steps (for reviewers):
```
git checkout -b fix/deps/grpc-jwt-2024\# make changes
make ci && go test ./...
git commit -am "chore: update grpc and jwt to mitigate CVE-2024-XXXX"
git push origin fix/deps/grpc-jwt-2024
```

tyler-sre: add note: also ensure we pin transitive module versions if CI shows mismatches. some services vendor dependencies; watch for go.sum diffs.

maria-engsec: @deploy-bot can you schedule the canary for tomorrow 09:00 UTC once PRs are merged?

deploy-bot: scheduled canary window for 2024-06-14 09:00 UTC. Notifying oncall.

jessica-legal: once deploys start, post compliance ticket and link PRs so we have an audit trail.

sam-runtime: quick QA checklist: smoke load at 10-20% of normal qps, iterate; check auth flow and long-lived streams specifically.

ashley-pm: thumbs if ready. :thumbsup:

maria-engsec: thumbs up. I'll open the umbrella incident channel and add links to PRs + CVE advisories. tagging folks for follow-up post-rollout for postmortem if needed.

nate-eng: will mock a rollback playbook in the PR description.

maria-engsec: thanks team. assigning owners in the incident channel.

(links: grpc advisory https://groups.google.com/g/grpc-announce, jwt advisory https://github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/security/advisories, govulncheck docs https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck)
